insight.title: Why Removing Steps Makes You More Creative
insight.subtitle: How deleting a step solves problems faster than adding one

sections.text: Look at the most iconic products you own. Their biggest breakthroughs often didn't come from adding new features, but from removing them. We naturally favor addition, yet the most elegant innovation is usually subtraction.
Our brains are biologically biased to suggest more of something to fix a problem. We buy organizers for clutter or create rules for efficiency. Real creativity begins when you resist the urge to add.

Great decisions aren't made by considering every possible option, but by stripping away the noise. When you remove the non-essential, the best path forward finally becomes visible, allowing you to move much faster.
Try this today: When you face a complex task today, identify one step you can skip to reach the goal.
Innovation isn't what you build; it's what you have the courage to remove.
